label: KEATING // JUDGEMENTS
format: explainer — numbered three-step diagram, 'how it works'

tts.instructions: Voice: a warm, grounded teacher who genuinely likes their students. Tone: calm, curious and a little wry; never salesy. Pacing: unhurried and conversational, with a small breath at each em dash and a real pause after questions. Pronounce 'Keating' as KEE-ting.

scenes.text: Step one: your answer comes first. It's saved — with the question and the task — before any review begins.
Step two: an independent judge checks it against the rubric.
Step three: the result lands beside your work, with a reason you can open. If the review missed something, flag it.
Judgements also decide what you practise next — tuned on two hundred and eighty-eight practice states.
A second opinion — not the final word. Keating: judgement you can check.
